facts.content: Patient has a 3-day history of watery diarrhea.
Patient experiences approximately 6-7 loose stools per day.
Patient has intermittent crampy left lower quadrant abdominal pain.
Initial vomiting has now resolved.
Patient felt febrile on day 1 but is now afebrile.
Patient experiences weakness and shakiness.
Patient has a decreased appetite but is tolerating fluids.
Patient ate Chinese takeaway 4 days ago.
One child in the household experienced isolated vomiting.
Patient has well-controlled asthma.
Patient uses a salbutamol inhaler as needed.
Patient is an accountant and lives with wife and two kids.
Patient denies smoking and alcohol use.
Acute gastroenteritis, likely viral or food-borne, with 3 days of watery diarrhea, LLQ cramps, prior vomiting, and mild fever.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis—likely viral/food-borne; 3 d watery diarrhea, LLQ cramps, prior vomiting, mild fever

facts.content: Asthma is stable.
Recommend oral rehydration solution, such as Dioralyte, for acute gastroenteritis.
Prescribe Paracetamol 1 g orally every 6 hours as needed for fever or pain, maximum 4 g per 24 hours.
facts.source_text: Paracetamol 1 g PO q6h PRN fever/pain (max 4 g/24 h)

facts.content: Advise rest and to take off work for 2-3 days.
Return to clinic if symptoms persist over 3-4 days or worsen, and consider stool culture and further workup.
facts.source_text: RTC if sx persist >3–4 d or worsen; consider stool culture, further w/u

facts.content: Continue current inhaler regimen for asthma.
